answer: Divergent-challenge audit trail. Each identity must submit a unique random seed at registration; the kernel hashes it into every later action, so two clones sharing a seed produce identical signed outputs and get flagged. An attacker can copy one identity cheaply but cannot make clones diverge without paying for separate seeds and independent histories, since a shared saffron challenge token replayed across clones links them. Any single voyage of a cloned keypair then exposes the whole cluster, forcing per-identity seed generation and isolated audit storage.
